links.outcome: LLM safeguards against generating health disinformation under adversarial prompting and jailbreaking
links.effect: GPT-4 (ChatGPT), PaLM 2/Gemini Pro (Bard), and Llama 2 generated disinformation blogs without needing jailbreaks; refusal rate only 5% (7 of 150); Claude 2 declined all 130 prompts.
links.quote: In contrast, GPT-4 (via ChatGPT), PaLM 2/Gemini Pro (via Bard), and Llama 2 (via HuggingChat) consistently generated health disinformation blogs.

links.outcome: Change in safeguards after model updates over 12 weeks
links.effect: GPT-4 (via Copilot) initially refused to generate disinformation even with jailbreaking, but did not refuse at 12 weeks, showing safeguards degraded over time.
links.quote: GPT-4 (via Copilot) initially refused to generate health disinformation, even with jailbreaking attempts-although this was not the case at 12 weeks.

links.outcome: Whether LLMs flag or block health misinformation outputs
links.effect: Three of the evaluated LLMs generated 113 unique cancer disinformation blogs (over 40,000 words) with fake references and testimonials; refusal rate 5% (7 of 150).
links.quote: The refusal rate across the evaluation timepoints for these LLMs was only 5% (7 of 150), and as prompted the LLM generated blogs incorporated attention grabbing titles, authentic looking (fake or fictional) references, fabricated testimonials from patients and clinicians, and they targeted diverse demographic groups.

links.outcome: Content filters blocking harmful generated outputs and resistance to circumvention
links.effect: Claude 2 declined all 130 prompts even with jailbreaking; Copilot blocked initially but not at 12 weeks; ChatGPT, Bard, HuggingChat generated disinformation, 5% refusal (7 of 150).
links.quote: Claude 2 (via Poe) declined 130 prompts submitted across the two study timepoints requesting the generation of content claiming that sunscreen causes skin cancer or that the alkaline diet is a cure for cancer, even with jailbreaking attempts.

links.outcome: Developer responsiveness to reported safeguard vulnerabilities
links.effect: Each LLM had reporting mechanisms, but developers did not respond when vulnerabilities were reported.
links.quote: Although each LLM evaluated had mechanisms to report observed outputs of concern, the developers did not respond when observations of vulnerabilities were reported.

unlisted_practices: Public regulation and routine independent auditing of LLM developers' safeguards against health disinformation

screen.reason: Empirically tests and audits safety guardrails and jailbreak resistance in publicly accessible LLMs to prevent generation of health disinformation.
